Happy exploring, travelers!

notes.title: Playtest the huge new Out There: Oceans of Time 1.2 Update on September 7!
notes.content:
Since the release of [b]Out There: Oceans of Time,[/b] we have been working hard to prepare our biggest update to the game to date; a huge 1.2 featuring a complete overhaul of Expeditions and a full rebalancing of the game. 

We want the game to be the best it can be, and to achieve that, we’re bringing you into the heart of the process.

We've listened to your feedback, notes and suggestions, and have reworked the game to meet your ongoing expectations. 

You will experience a taste of these reworks during an exclusive test phase next week, taking the form of a private playtest. For those of you that own the game already, details om how to access the playtest will be shared on September 7th. 

Questions? We’ve got answers!

[b]* Who is the playtest for?[/b]
All players who already have the game in their Steam library will be able to access the 1.2 Update branch. 

[b]* What does the playtest involve?[/b]
The playtest will offer up the brand new Expedition system, in addition to a rehauled and rebalanced version of the game. 

[b]* How?[/b]
Unlike starting a fresh game, you won’t start at the beginning of the story, but further into the journey, with a pre-defined crew and cargo. 

[b]* Why?[/b]
The objective of the test is to get your feedback and feelings in order to validate and finalize the latest changes to the game before they’re rolled out. This is a unique chance for you to participate in the finalization of the game; we’re very excited to hear your thoughts, feedback and comments. 

[b]* When?[/b]
Get your diary! On September 7th the playtest branch will open its doors to all players. 

--

notes.title: Thank you for your feedback!
notes.content:
Out There: Oceans of Time landed on Steam yesterday! 

We have been reading your feedback and we want to say thank you for it. We have been made aware that there are bugs cropping up for players in the launch build. We're sorry for how these issues have affected your experience at launch and we will be solving these problems as soon as possible.

Today we're putting out the first small patch to fix some issues you have been encountering. Right now we are reading every bug report and review you have left us to put together future patches. The best places for you to report issues and give feedback is on our Steam forums and Discord. 

Steam Forums: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1145290/discussions/

Discord (with bug tracker): https://discord.gg/7xwWGjKTfQ

We hear your design feedback and have ideas to address it. However, our first priority is making sure every player has a smooth stable experience, across languages.

[list]
[*] Fixed Simplified Chinese version : the game should now run properly
[*] Fixed a bug vanishing the items acquired during trading
[*] Fixed a bug preventing to travel to an Epsilon system previously visited
[*] Fixed various typos in the dialogues
[*] Removed ‘beta’ mention from the title screen
[/list]

Thank you for your support, we want to do right by our fans and give you the experience you've been waiting for. 

- Mi-Clos Studios & Modern Wolf

notes.title: Discover and explore planets in Out There: Oceans of Time
notes.content:
In [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i], you can go on expeditions to discover [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1145290/view/5216827407350277790]different biomes[/url]. This additional feature allows you to manage your crew members and hone in on their specialities. It is unlike spatial exploration where you manage resources.



Going into an expedition allows you to progress the [b]story[/b], attempt new [b]missions [/b]and level up your [b]crew members[/b].

Gather [b]additional resources[/b], necessary to [b]build new modules and technologies[/b] on your spaceship. You can also [b]trade [/b]them using the barter system in villages and inhabited planets.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/d2b05352a1ffd3526d9124a4926361a5661062ab.png[/img]

To attempt an expedition, you need to [b]scan a planet[/b] to reveal any  anomalies. repare your team composed of 4 crew members and send them out to explore the planet.

Each member possesses their own [b]class[/b], [b]health points[/b], [b]action points[/b] and [b]competences[/b]. Those statistics are created randomly when the character is generated, they will vary depending on their class, rarity and can be upgraded when the character levels up. 

Crew members all possess [b]action points[/b]. You need to manage them carefully as once you run out, you won’t be able to use the character’s [b]competences [/b]or make [b]choices [/b]during the story.   During the story you can obtain  [b]bonuses[/b] and [b]rewards[/b], which can be new crew members or unlocking a new story point. 

Once your team is ready, you can go explore! You will discover [b]new biomes[/b] and randomized [b]maps [/b]each time you attempt an expedition and you will encounter hazards: from the environment and story events. They can affect your party by giving them maluses or bonuses. Hence why the creation of your party is so important.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/19b8dbfbf737f53e583253d69d2b6f3690b86b2e.png[/img]


Will you be able to gear up your party to succeed in your expeditions?
Find out this spring!

notes.title: Manage your ship and resources in Out There: Oceans of Time
notes.content:
In our previous posts, we showcased [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1145290/announcements/detail/5076095625049590054]several spaceships[/url] you will find in [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i].

Today, let’s see how to manage our spaceships from the inside! Let’s head to the cargo!



Your spaceship requires a [b]management of resources[/b] to help you survive in space. At the same time, you need to [b]manage your crew[/b] and make sure they are happy. Finally, it is important to aim to improve the [b]technologies [/b]inside the ship.

What are those resources and what are they used for?

First, your crew needs [b]oxygen[/b]. [b]Garden Planets[/b] are quite an easy resource to find it as they are full of it.
Secondly, to travel further, your ship will need to fuel. When running low, create some using  [b]Hydrogen [/b]or [b]Helium[/b]. You can find those elements on [b]Gaz Planets[/b] and [b]stars[/b].
Finally, as you travel, your space ship will get damaged. To continue on your voyage you will have to repair it by using [b]Iron[/b]. You will find Iron on [b]Rock Planets[/b].

You will need all those resources and more to continue your space travel. It is crucial to [b]manage [/b]them as the difficulty will increase and those resources become more valuable as the story progresses.  You will also need to pay attention to the space they take on your spaceship, as you have a [b]limited amount of slots[/b] in it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/d713ca1666b0b05e6063a0f09f74ae61499df0f0.gif[/img]


Resources aren’t the only thing you will need to keep an eye on. On the other side, you will need to satisfy the needs of your crew: their [b]morale [/b]and [b]comfort[/b]. 
It is a new feature compared to [i]Out There[/i]. 
Comfort influences your crew’s morale: the better, the merrier they will be. If morale is too low, some crew members will leave , creating unpredictable events that might affect your travel.

To[b] increase comfort[/b], you will need to construct [b]modules [/b]such as the [i]Relaxation Pod[/i], the [i]Regular Cabin[/i] or the [i]Mess Hall[/i]. This will allow your crew to gather together around a good meal with galactic views. 

To create those modules, you will need to find blueprints of them. Stock the necessary materials and construct them on specific slots of your spaceship. You can also disassemble them and repair them.




Now, you know how to manage your resources and crew! However there is one last crucial element to consider in your ship: [b]technologies[/b]. 
They work like modules however they add a [b]new functionality[/b] to the ship, such as: the ability to travel further thanks to the [i]Subspace Reactor[/i], prob Rock Planets and Garden Planets with the [i]Driller [/i]or gather resources from stars with the [i]Ultraprobe[/i]. 
They will be helpful to continue your journey through galaxies.

Some of those technologies can be upgraded when they are [b]placed next to one another[/b] creating a [b]Synergy [/b]effect. Keep in mind the specific arrangement of technologies might create new ones and make them better.[i] Interplanetary Propulsion[/i] is most effective when placed next to [i]Solar Sails[/i]. Same for [i]Shield Generator[/i] which is more resistant adjacent to [i]Void Fluctuation Projector[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/5c3c38bd1f6e769b29fd8a61e83d2b0269df8c8c.jpg[/img]


In [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i] you will find mechanics from [i]Out There[/i] with some brand new ones such as crew management and modules.

Will you be able to manage your spaceship and crew?
Find out this Spring!

notes.title: Survive in space within Out There: Oceans of Time
notes.content:
In [i]Out There: Oceans of Time[/i] you will get the opportunity to navigate through space to complete [b][url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1145290/announcements/detail/3031453686300710711]Nyx’ mission[/url][/b] and [b]explore this endless horizon to survive[/b].


Spatial exploration will lead you from one place to another in hopes of [b]retrieving resources[/b]. However, all planets don’t offer the same kind of earnings. [b]Rocky planets[/b] will provide you with [b]Iron[/b], while [b]garden planets[/b] will offer [b]Oxygen[/b]. Retrieve these valuable resources by going on expeditions or finding places to forage for them. 
[b]Gas planets[/b] can't be scouted but you can probe them to collect [b]Hydrogen[/b] and [b]Helium[/b], much like what you would expect to find inside stars. But be careful when probing those! They are highly unstable and will threaten the integrity of your spaceship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/bbe2d3efb8dd504ca492f3a92338cd997b330530.png[/img]

In your journey, you will encounter [b]civilized planets[/b]. Just like [b]villages in garden planets[/b], you can [b]trade resources[/b] with the local alien inhabitants  through a bartering system. During those exchanges, you can also find [b]technologies[/b], [b]modules[/b] and [b]skills[/b] for your crew. That’s not all, you might also end up r[b]ecruiting a new alien[/b].
On those civilized planets, you can meet [b]other ethnicities[/b]. They speak the [b]language of the Gods[/b]. You can learn various words from events in-game to better [b]communicate[/b] with aliens and obtain bonuses.


During your exploration, you may come across [b]black holes[/b]. You can only conquer them if you have the right technology. Scavenge [b]abandoned ships[/b] and  participate in [b]narrative events[/b] and discover more about Nyx and Sergeï’s grand quest within the [i]Out There[/i] universe.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35677524/66968c0ae1791eba417e9e46fa44f6b8fe874f91.jpg[/img]

Space is dangerous and your choices have consequences. You can only count on yourself to survive!

Join the adventure on the 7th of April.

notes.content:
Space folder drives are spun up and a new destination has been set. We're delighted to announce that [b]Out There: Oceans of Time[/b] will be dropping into your orbit on [b]February 10th, 2022.[/b]

The release date was announced exclusively during the MIX Next showcase that aired over the weekend, dropping in our brand new [b]"Across Space and Time"[/b] trailer that tracks the origins of the Out There franchise right up until today, and the upcoming release of Oceans of Time (with all new gameplay footage!). 

Have a look:

[previewyoutube=2XssgE4GcB0;full][/previewyoutube]

For those new to the (many) worlds of Out There, Oceans of Time is the sequel to Out There, the award-winning space exploration game blending roguelike, resource management, and interactive fiction (but you don't need to have played the original to enjoy this new adventure). Explore a vast universe that is different every time you play, and immerse yourself in a rich, branching narrative where the very fate of the cosmos rests in the hands of you and your crew.

notes.content:

notes.title: Announcing Silmaris: Dice Kingdom
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/7403583/582aefedf446fd671498187cb4cdd944c287bda0.jpg[/img]

[h1]Roll the dice for Silmaris![/h1]

Have you ever dream of ruling your kingdom... with dice? That's exactly what Silmaris offer in this medieval narrative-driven management game. 

Take the helm of the fallen city of Thylla and restore the lost power of your kingdom by subduing the other monarchs in the valley. Choose and use your advisors wisely to wage war or form alliances, develop trade and explore the world, or spy on your enemies and conspire to overthrow the other rulers!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steam/apps/1293120/ss_5e9a8e1b12a20c3d7519a0d164045dd730f79962.1920x1080.jpg[/img]
[h1]Roll the dice for Silmaris![/h1]

Each new game features a different story packed with twists and turns. React to events and make the right decisions when fate thwarts your reign… and as you prepare to face the greatest threat the world has ever known!

Silmaris: Dice Kingdom will be available this year on PC (Win, Mac, Linux).

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1293120/
